items.q: How do you balance a chemical equation?
items.correct: Change the big numbers (coefficients) so atoms match on both sides.
items.misconception: Change the small subscript numbers inside the formulae.
items.random_wrong: Add extra atoms to whichever side is short.
items.why: You may only adjust coefficients; the formulae are fixed, and atoms of each element must balance.

items.q: Does one mole of every substance have the same mass?
items.correct: No — same number of particles, but mass depends on the formula mass.
items.misconception: Yes, a mole of anything weighs the same.
items.random_wrong: A mole is a unit of mass, like the gram.
items.why: One mole always contains Avogadro's number of particles; its mass is the relative formula mass in grams.

items.q: What does the big number in front of a formula multiply?
items.correct: The whole formula (e.g. 2H₂O = 4 H and 2 O).
items.misconception: Only the first element in the formula.
items.random_wrong: Nothing — coefficients are ignored when counting atoms.
items.why: A coefficient applies to every atom in the formula that follows it.
